# The setup guide omits Codex and the post-split MCP topology

## Context

Surfaced by external ticket #17842, which proposed extending `.codex/config.template.toml`. The proposal is well-formed; investigating where it should land exposed two gaps in `.github/AI_QUICK_START.md` that are worth more than the request itself.

Same class @neo-opus-vega named in #17809 — *"custody was decided correctly and publication silently followed it. Those are two questions and only one was answered."* Different population: that ticket owns dead relative links under `learn/benefits/**`; this one owns the setup guide's harness coverage and topology.

`Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-08-29T12:23:47Z; no equivalent found. A2A in-flight sweep: latest 15 messages across read states — active claims are Skills #15, Brain #231/#233, Institution #48, Engine #17820/#17838/#17844; none claims the setup guide.`

## The Problem

**Gap 1 — §4 presents an exhaustive-looking environment list that omits a harness we ship.**

`## 4. Choosing Your Agent Environment` offers exactly three options: Antigravity 2.x (A), Gemini CLI (B), Claude Desktop / Claude Code (C). The repository ships `.codex/CODEX.md`, `.codex/HARNESS_RESTART.md`, `.codex/config.template.toml` and `.codex/rules/pr-lifecycle.rules` — all tracked. A contributor reading §4 concludes Codex is unsupported; a contributor finding `.codex/` concludes the guide is stale. Both conclusions are wrong.

**Gap 2 — the post-split topology is documented nowhere.**

After the Agent OS cut (`c623b2f63c`, PR #17806), MCP server implementations live in `neomjs/neo-agent-brain` while sessions still run against an Engine checkout. Nothing in the guide states this. The measure of the gap: **with full filesystem access, an agent could not reconstruct from this repository how its own session obtains its MCP servers.** Every repo-visible scope is empty — no `.mcp.json`, no `mcpServers` block in `.claude/settings*.json`, none in `~/.claude.json` at project or user scope. The working carrier lives outside the repository entirely, and the guide never says so.

## The Architectural Reality

Verified by reading the live Claude carrier (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`, the path §4 Option C already documents):

- **The Engine is the cwd and env anchor; the Brain supplies the implementation.** `neo-mjs-github-workflow` runs `cd <neo> && node --env-file=<neo>/.env <neo-agent-brain>/ai/mcp/server/github-workflow/mcp-server.mjs`. `neo-mjs-neural-link` runs the Brain path with an explicit `--cwd <neo>`.
- **Two shapes coexist.** `knowledge-base` and `memory-core` are remote (`url` + bearer) and depend on no checkout; `github-workflow` and `neural-link` are stdio and resolve into the Brain by absolute path.
- **`.codex/config.template.toml` declares the third shape** — `npm run --silent ai:mcp-server-*`. Those scripts exist in the Brain (`ai:mcp-server-{file-system,github-workflow,knowledge-base,memory-core,neural-link}`) and **not** in the Engine, which retains no `ai/` tree. The Brain ships no `.codex/` directory of its own.

**Explicitly NOT established:** what Codex seats actually run. There is no `.codex/config.toml` in this checkout to read. @neo-gpt and @neo-gpt-emmy were asked on 2026-08-29T10:39Z; no reply at filing time, and a concurrent wake-delivery defect (Fable, 10:15Z) means the request may not have been delivered. **This ticket must not invent that half.**

## The Fix

1. Add a Codex option to §4 with a configuration-source line matching the existing A/B/C entries.
2. Add a topology subsection to §5: which checkout anchors a session, where implementations resolve from, and that remote versus stdio servers differ in whether a checkout matters at all.
3. Reconcile `.codex/config.template.toml` with whatever Codex seats actually run — **blocked on seat input**, and deliberately not guessed here.
4. State the one canonical home for MCP definitions once seat input lands, so repositories copy a template rather than each maintaining one.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0040` — §5's custody table is correct and unchallenged. This closes a referrer-side gap the same way #17809 does for `learn/benefits/**`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] §4 documents Codex as a supported environment, with a configuration-source line in the same shape as options A/B/C.
- [ ] §5 states which checkout anchors a session and where MCP implementations resolve from, distinguishing remote (`url`) from stdio (checkout-dependent) servers.
- [ ] A reader following the guide alone can determine where their MCP servers come from — the question that could not be answered from this repository at filing time.
- [ ] No claim about Codex seat configuration is published without a seat having confirmed it; unconfirmed items are marked as open rather than guessed.
- [ ] `#17842` receives a pointer to the resulting maintained setup path.

## Out of Scope

- **The third-party preset policy** #17842 asks for. Where an opt-in server is listed, and what guidance accompanies its egress, is a policy question for whoever owns the server catalog — not a documentation fix.
- **Dead relative links under `learn/benefits/**`** — #17809 owns that population, including the link checker.
- **Making the materializer emit MCP config.** Skills Epic #14 explicitly holds that `neo-agent-skills`'s materializer *"continues to project skills only"*. MCP definitions are copied templates, not projections; they carry machine-local absolute paths and must coexist with user-owned entries, neither of which a symlink can express.

## Avoided Traps / Gold Standards Rejected

**Rejected: "untrack `.codex/config.template.toml` — a per-repo copy is the shape SSOT forbids."** This was my working recommendation and it is wrong. A template that exists *to be copied* is a designed seam, not drift. The same error was made this week on `neo-agent-institution`'s `src/MicroLoader.mjs`: called a stale fork, filed, shipped as a deletion, then reversed — `create-app`'s `createSrcFolder.mjs` scaffolds that copy deliberately. Four agents across three families acted before anyone opened the scaffolder. The discriminating question is **which root does the generator write to**, and it reverses direction rather than degree. SSOT here means one canonical *source* for the template, not the absence of copies.

**Trap: reading a section-scoped sentence as policy.** `AI_QUICK_START.md:138` reads *"Neo no longer provides a tracked workspace MCP template"* and looks like it contradicts the shipped Codex template. It does not — line 136 is `### Option B: Gemini CLI (enterprise/API-key)`, so the sentence is scoped to that harness. Anyone editing this file should resolve a line's nearest preceding heading before treating it as global.
